calls.thesis: The largest and most deliberately-constructed defined-risk directional print on today's tape: ~$19.8M of opening long put debit verticals across two consecutive expiries (Nov-20 and Dec-18, both P75/P67), struck 10.4% below spot, into a gold-miner ETF that closed $83.68 after +7.39% on the day and +13.74% over five sessions. Side resolution is unambiguous (99.8% ask on both long legs, 99.9% bid on both short legs) and v/OI of 4.4 and 10.6 confirms opening, not closing. The play type anchors to a post-hygiene term structure that is flat at 44-48% — which is precisely why a two-month ladder rather than a single event month is coherent, and why the Dec-18 kink was explicitly not treated as the trade. sector-rotation-strategist reached the same bearish conclusion through an entirely different lane (largest 5-day outflow in the 21-ETF universe at -$28.6M, ~$36M of put buying at ask against ~$11.5M of calls). Against that: repeat_count is 1, the 30d cum-flow is a MIXED -2.1% of gross, the OI build is two-sided and call-led, and a dated macro stack supports the rally rather than the fade. Scored 2 -> DROP, and routed watch_only as a directional short. The rubric correctly refuses to pay for what may simply be portfolio insurance.
